title: Anomalously fast heating of ground states in dephased $SU(N)$ spin systems
authors: Tairan Lou, Junxiao Chen, Xiang-Ping Jiang, Mingdi Xu, Lei Pan
abstract: We identify a strong quantum Mpemba effect in which a many-body ground state heats faster than every Gibbs state at finite positive temperature under the same dissipative dynamics within a fixed-color sector. In ferromagnetic $SU(N)$ exchange systems with local dephasing, exact coherence shells confine the ground-state evolution and exclude all slower Liouvillian modes. Its relaxation rate is fixed by the bath, independently of system size, exchange graph, and integrability. We derive an energy-resolved sign criterion that guarantees a slower thermal contribution throughout the positive-temperature range. An exact finite-chain solution proves this rate inversion, and symmetry-resolved calculations confirm the criterion in larger spin-one chains, including nonintegrable exchange. The zero-temperature endpoint of a continuous Gibbs family can therefore be dynamically isolated by its exact exclusion from slow relaxation channels.
summary: This paper studies the non-equilibrium dynamics of dephased SU(N) spin systems, revealing a strong quantum Mpemba effect. It proves that the ground state heats up anomalously fast compared to any finite-temperature Gibbs state. The findings establish a robust, size-independent rate separation between the ground state and thermal relaxation channels.
main_problem: The paper investigates an anomalous quantum Mpemba effect, where the ground state of a many-body system heats faster than any finite-temperature Gibbs state under specific dissipative dynamics.
main_result: The ground state evolution rate is fixed by the bath and is shown to be strictly faster than the thermal relaxation rate for positive temperatures, demonstrating a rate inversion.
method: The analysis uses the Lindblad master equation formalism, deriving exact solutions for the ground state evolution via a 'shell identity' and employing spectral projection methods to compare decay rates.
model_or_system: The system is a ferromagnetic SU(N) exchange chain subjected to local color dephasing, modeled by a Hamiltonian and a Lindblad dissipator. The dynamics are analyzed within a fixed-color sector.
key_observables: Trace distance ($D_{tr}(t)$) and normalized energy deviation ($E_ eta(t)$) are used to quantify the rate of relaxation and heating.
important_parameters: The dephasing rate ($\gamma$), the temperature parameter ($ eta$), and the exchange couplings ($J_1, J_2$) are key parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis is restricted to a fixed-color sector, and the rate comparison relies on establishing a sign criterion for the thermal contribution.
figures_summary: Figures compare the energy deviation and trace distance for the ground state versus various finite temperatures, visually confirming the ground state's faster decay rate.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from identifying the anomalous heating effect to deriving the exact ground-state evolution using shell identities, establishing the rate separation via spectral analysis, and confirming the results with specific observable measurements.
why_interesting: This work provides a rigorous theoretical demonstration of non-equilibrium dynamics where the zero-temperature limit exhibits unique, faster relaxation dynamics compared to thermal ensembles, which is highly relevant to understanding thermalization in open quantum systems.
